metadata.title: A two-grid method for the $C^0$ interior penalty discretization of the Monge-Amp\`ere equation

extraction_notes.note: The introduction both defines $A'$ and states its value at $u$, which (3.2) restates; the sentence was kept as the only definition of $A'$, and (3.2) is the node for the property.
Numbered equations (2.1) and (2.5) are named cited results (inverse estimates, interpolation properties), so they were retyped theorem/external instead of equation.
Lemma 3.1 (reproved 'for the convenience of the reader', from Brenner et al. p. 5) and Theorem 3.7 (the H^1 estimate of Brenner et al., given a new proof) are marked external; their proofs are paper.
The two-grid algorithm is an enumerate in running text after a bold heading (the declared alg environment is unused); it was extracted as a prose algorithm with two unmarked steps.
Tables 1-2 of H^1 errors, rates and timings are not nodes; the numerical conclusions are recorded in the claim and remark of Section 5. Motivational discussion in the introduction is not extracted.
The paragraph after (2.27) argues the bound on $G^z_h$ without a proof label; it was taken as the prose proof of a claim formed by the sentence holding (2.27).

nodes.name: Elliptic Monge-Ampère equation (Dirichlet problem)
nodes.statement: \det (D^2 u) = f \text{ in } \Omega, \quad u=g \text{ on } \partial \Omega,
nodes.statement_short: Dirichlet problem $\det D^2u=f$ in $\Omega$, $u=g$ on $\partial\Omega$.
nodes.label: MA

nodes.name: Convex polygonal domain and strictly convex smooth solution
nodes.statement: The domain $\Omega$ is assumed to be a convex polygonal domain of $\mathbb{R}^2$ and \eqref{MA} is assumed to have a strictly convex smooth solution $u \in C^3(\tir{\Omega})$.

nodes.name: Regularity and positivity of the data f and g
nodes.statement: The function $f \in C^1(\tir{\Omega})$ is given and satisfies $f \geq c_0$ for a constant $c_0 >0$ and the function $g\in C(\partial \Omega)$ is also given and assumed to extend to a $C^3(\tir{\Omega})$ function $G$.

nodes.name: Hessian matrix and determinant operator
nodes.statement: In \eqref{MA}, $D^2 u=\big( \partial^2 u/(\partial x_i \partial x_j)\big)_{i,j=1,\ldots, 2} $ is the Hessian matrix of $u$ and $\det$ denotes the determinant operator.

nodes.name: Lagrange finite element space $V_h$
nodes.statement: Let $V_h$ denote the Lagrange finite element space of degree $k \geq 2$ and let $D v$ denote the gradient of the function $v$.

nodes.name: Cofactor matrix
nodes.statement: Recall that $\operatorname{cof} D^2 v$ denotes the matrix of cofactors of $D^2 v$.

nodes.name: C^0 interior penalty discretization of the Monge-Ampère equation
nodes.statement: The $C^0$ interior penalty discretization can be written in abstract form as: find $u_h \in V_h$ such that $u_h=g_h$ on $\partial \Omega$ and \begin{align} A(u_h,\phi) & = 0, \forall \phi \in V_h \cap H_0^1(\Omega). \end{align} Here $g_h$ denotes the canonical interpolant in $V_h$ of a continuous extension of $g$ and $A$ is defined in \eqref{IP-form} below.
nodes.statement_short: Find $u_h\in V_h$ with $u_h=g_h$ on $\partial\Omega$ and $A(u_h,\phi)=0$ for all test functions.

nodes.name: Abstract interior penalty discrete problem
nodes.statement: A(u_h,\phi) & = 0, \forall \phi \in V_h \cap H_0^1(\Omega).
nodes.label: IP-abstract

nodes.name: Fréchet derivative $A'(u;v,\phi)$ of the interior penalty form
nodes.statement: The discretization has the property that if we denote by $A'(u;v, \phi)$ the Fr\'echet derivative evaluated at $u$ of the mapping $v \to A(v,\phi)$, then $A'(u;v,\phi)= \int_{\Omega} \big( (\operatorname{cof} D^2 u) D v \big) \cdot D \phi \,d x,$ which gives the weak form of a standard linear elliptic operator.
nodes.statement_short: $A'(u;v,\phi)$ is the Fréchet derivative at $u$ of $v\mapsto A(v,\phi)$, equal to the weak form of a linear elliptic operator.

nodes.name: Existence of smooth solutions on smooth strictly convex domains
nodes.statement: It is known that when $\Omega$ is strictly convex with a smooth boundary, and with our smoothness assumptions on $f$ and $g$, \eqref{MA} has a smooth solution.
assumptions: $\Omega$ is strictly convex with a smooth boundary
with our smoothness assumptions on $f$ and $g$

nodes.name: Triangulation $\mathcal{T}_h$
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{T}_h$ denote a conforming, shape regular and quasi-uniform triangulation of $\Omega$ into simplices $K$.

nodes.name: Edge sets $\mathcal{E}_h$, $\mathcal{E}^b_h$, $\mathcal{E}^i_h$
nodes.statement: We denote by $\mathcal{E}_h$ the set of edges of $\mathcal{T}_h$, by $\mathcal{E}^b_h$ the set of boundary edges and by $\mathcal{E}^i_h$ the set of interior edges.

nodes.name: Element diameter $h_K$ and mesh size $h$
nodes.statement: Let $h_K$ denote the diameter of the element $K$ and put $h=\max_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h} h_K$.

nodes.name: Mesh size bounded by one
nodes.statement: We assume that $0< h \leq 1$.

nodes.name: Shape regularity and quasi-uniformity constants
nodes.statement: We recall that, for a shape regular and quasi-uniform triangulation, there exists a constant $\sigma >0$ such that $h_K/\rho_K \leq \sigma$, for all $K \in \mathcal{T}_h$ where $\rho_K$ denotes the radius of the largest ball inside $K$ and there is another constant $C$ such that $h \leq C h_K$ for all $K \in \mathcal{T}_h$.
assumptions: for a shape regular and quasi-uniform triangulation
conclusions: there exists a constant $\sigma >0$ such that $h_K/\rho_K \leq \sigma$, for all $K \in \mathcal{T}_h$
there is another constant $C$ such that $h \leq C h_K$ for all $K \in \mathcal{T}_h$

nodes.name: Sobolev spaces $W^{s,p}(\Omega)$
nodes.statement: We use the usual notation $W^{s,p}(\Omega)$, $1 \leq s, p \leq \infty$ for the Sobolev spaces of functions in $L^{p}(\Omega)$, $1 \leq p \leq \infty$, with weak derivatives up to order $s$ in $L^{p}(\Omega)$.
differentia: with weak derivatives up to order $s$ in $L^{p}(\Omega)$

nodes.name: Spaces $H^s(\Omega)$ and $H^1_0(\Omega)$
nodes.statement: The standard notation $H^s(\Omega)$ is used for $W^{s,2}(\Omega)$ and $H^{1}_{0}(\Omega)$ denotes the subspace of elements in $H^1(\Omega)$ with vanishing trace on the boundary $\partial \Omega$.
differentia: with vanishing trace on the boundary $\partial \Omega$

nodes.name: Space $W^{1,\infty}_0(\Omega)$
nodes.statement: Similarly, we define $W^{1,\infty}_{0}(\Omega)$.

nodes.name: Sobolev norm and seminorm
nodes.statement: The norm of $v \in W^{k,p}(\Omega)$ is denoted $\|v\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}$ and its seminorm $|v|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}$.

nodes.name: Broken Sobolev norm
nodes.statement: We will need the broken Sobolev norm defined for $1 \leq p < \infty$ by \begin{equation*} \|v\|_{W^{k,p}({\mathcal T}_h)}=\left(\sum_{K \in {\mathcal T}_h}\|v\|_{W^{k,p}(K)}^p\right)^{1/p}, \end{equation*} and for $p=\infty$ by \begin{equation*} \|v\|_{W^{k,\infty}({\mathcal T}_h)}=\max_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h}\|v\|_{W^{k,\infty}(K)}. \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: $\|v\|_{W^{k,p}(\mathcal T_h)}$ is the $\ell^p$ (or max) combination of elementwise $W^{k,p}$ norms.

nodes.name: Inverse estimates
nodes.statement: \|v\|_{W^{s,p}(\mathcal{T}_h)}\leq Ch^{t-s+\min(0,\frac{2}{p}-\frac{2}{q})}\|v\|_{W^{t,q}(\mathcal{T}_h)}, \forall v\in V_h,
nodes.statement_short: Finite element functions satisfy inverse estimates trading derivatives and integrability for powers of $h$.
nodes.label: inverse

nodes.name: Trace inequality
nodes.statement: We also recall the trace inequality \cite[Theorem 1.6.6]{Brenner08}, $\|v\|_{L^p(\partial \Omega)}\leq C \|v\|_{W^{1,p}(\Omega)}, 1 \leq p \leq \infty$ which gives by a scaling argument \begin{equation} \|v\|_{L^p(\partial K)}\leq C h^{-\frac{1}{p}} (||v||_{L^p(K)} + h ||D v||_{L^p(K)} ). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Trace inequality $\|v\|_{L^p(\partial\Omega)}\le C\|v\|_{W^{1,p}}$ and its scaled elementwise form.

nodes.name: Scaled elementwise trace estimate
nodes.statement: \|v\|_{L^p(\partial K)}\leq C h^{-\frac{1}{p}} (||v||_{L^p(K)} + h ||D v||_{L^p(K)} ).
nodes.label: trace-estimate

nodes.name: Sum of edge $L^1$ norms bounded by $W^{1,1}$ norm
nodes.statement: \sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}_h^i} \|\phi\|_{L^1(e)} \leq C h^{-1} \sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h}\|\phi\|_{W^{1,1}(K)} =C h^{-1} \|\phi\|_{W^{1,1}}.
nodes.label: w11-phi

nodes.name: Trace inverse inequality
nodes.statement: ||v||_{L^2(\partial K)} \leq C h^{-\frac{1}{2}} ||v||_{L^2(K)} \, \forall v \in V_h.
nodes.label: trace-inverse

nodes.name: Lagrange interpolation error estimate
nodes.statement: ||v-I_h v||_{W^{s,p}(\mathcal{T}_h)} & \leq C h^{k+1-s} ||v||_{W^{k+1,p}}, s=0, 1, 2 \text{ and } 1\leq p \leq \infty, v \in W^{k+1,p}.
nodes.statement_short: Lagrange interpolation error is $O(h^{k+1-s})$ in broken $W^{s,p}$ norms.
nodes.label: nodal-interpolant

nodes.name: Proof of the interpolation estimate (2.5)
nodes.statement: This follows from our assumptions on the triangulation and \cite[ (4.4.5) ]{Brenner08}, i.e. for $ v \in W^{k+1,p}(K)$ \begin{equation} |v-I_h v|_{W^{s,p}(K)} \leq C h^{k+1-s}_K |v|_{W^{k+1,p}(K)}, s=0, 1, 2 \text{ and } 1\leq p \leq \infty. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Sum the local Bramble-Hilbert interpolation estimate (2.6) over shape-regular, quasi-uniform elements.

nodes.name: Local Lagrange interpolation estimate
nodes.statement: |v-I_h v|_{W^{s,p}(K)} \leq C h^{k+1-s}_K |v|_{W^{k+1,p}(K)}, s=0, 1, 2 \text{ and } 1\leq p \leq \infty.
nodes.label: local-nodal-interpolant

nodes.name: Boundary estimate for the gradient of the interpolation error
nodes.statement: \begin{split} || D( I_h u - u) ||_{L^{2}(\partial K)} & \leq C h^{- \frac{1}{2} } || D( I_h u - u) ||_{L^{2}(K)} + C h^{ \frac{1}{2} } || D(I_h u - u) ||_{H^{1}(K)} \\ & \leq C h^{k- \frac{1}{2}} || u ||_{H^{k+1}(K)}. \end{split}
nodes.label: bramble

nodes.name: Frobenius inner product
nodes.statement: For two matrices $A$ and $B$, $A:B = \sum^2_{i,j=1}A_{ij}B_{ij}$ denotes their Frobenius inner product.

nodes.name: Divergence of a matrix field
nodes.statement: The divergence of a matrix field is understood as the vector obtained by taking the divergence of each row.

nodes.name: Determinant via cofactor matrix
nodes.statement: \det D^2 v = \frac{1}{2} (\operatorname{cof} D^2 v): D^2 v,
nodes.label: det1

nodes.name: Fréchet derivative of the Monge-Ampère operator
nodes.statement: F'(v) w = (\operatorname{cof} D^2 v): D^2 w,
nodes.label: det3

nodes.name: Divergence identity for the cofactor matrix
nodes.statement: \operatorname{div}\big((\operatorname{cof} D^2 w) D v )= (\operatorname{cof} D^2 w): D^2 v,
nodes.label: det2

nodes.name: Divergence form of the linearized Monge-Ampère operator
nodes.statement: F'(u)v= \operatorname{div} \big((\operatorname{cof} D^2 u) D v \big).
nodes.label: det4

nodes.name: Linearity of the cofactor in two dimensions
nodes.statement: \operatorname{cof}(D^2 v +D^2 w) = \operatorname{cof}(D^2 v) + \operatorname{cof}(D^2 w),
nodes.label: linearity

nodes.name: Difference of determinants
nodes.statement: \det D^2 v - \det D^2 w = \frac{1}{2} (\operatorname{cof}(D^2 v) + \operatorname{cof}(D^2 w)): (D^2 v - D^2 w).
nodes.label: det5

nodes.name: Divergence form of the difference of determinants
nodes.statement: \det D^2 v - \det D^2 w = \frac{1}{2}\operatorname{div} \Big( \big( \operatorname{cof} D^2 (v+w)\big) D(v -w)\Big).
nodes.label: det6

nodes.name: Uniform positive definiteness of $\operatorname{cof} D^2 u$
nodes.statement: \alpha_0 |r|^2 \leq r^T (\operatorname{cof} D^2 u(x) ) r \leq \alpha_1 |r|^2, \quad \forall r \in \mathbb{R}^2.
nodes.label: SPD

nodes.name: Discrete (elementwise) Hessian
nodes.statement: For $v \in V_h$, we will make the abuse of notation of denoting by $D^2v$ the discrete Hessian of $v$ computed element by element.

nodes.name: Outward normal $n_K$ and restriction $v|_K$
nodes.statement: For $e \subset \partial K$, let $n_K$ denote the outward normal to $K$ and let $v|_K$ denote the restriction of the field $v$ to $K$.

nodes.name: Jump and average of a vector field
nodes.statement: For $e=K^+ \cap K^-$, we define the jump of the vector field $v$ across $e$ as \begin{equation} \[v\]_e=v|_{K^+} \cdot n_{K^+} + v|_{K^-} \cdot n_{K^-}, \end{equation} and its average on $e$ as \begin{equation} \{\!\{v\}\!\}_e= \frac{1}{2}(v|_{K^+} + v|_{K^-} ). \end{equation}

nodes.name: Jump and average of a matrix field
nodes.statement: The jump and average of a matrix field $E$ on $e$ are defined respectively as \begin{equation} \[E\]_e=n_{K^+}^T E|_{K^+} +n_{K^-}^T E|_{K^-}, \end{equation} and \begin{equation} \{\!\{E\}\!\}_e= \frac{1}{2}(E|_{K^+} + E|_{K^-}). \end{equation}
nodes.definiendum: jump and average of a matrix field

nodes.name: Projection $\hat{P}_h$ with respect to $A'(u;\cdot,\cdot)$
nodes.statement: Let $\hat{P}_h:H_0^1(\Omega) \rightarrow V_h$ denote the projection with respect to the bilinear form $A'(u;\cdot,\cdot)$ and recall that $G$ denotes a $C^3(\tir{\Omega})$ extension of $g$.
differentia: with respect to the bilinear form $A'(u;\cdot,\cdot)$

nodes.name: Ritz-type projection $P_h u$
nodes.statement: We define $$ P_h u = \hat{P}_h(u-G) + I_h G, $$ where $I_h$ denotes the canonical Lagrange interpolant operator into $V_h$.

nodes.name: Defining relation of $P_h u$
nodes.statement: A'(u;P_h u - u, \phi) = A'(u;I_h G - G, \phi) ,~ \forall \phi \in V_h \cap H_0^1(\Omega).
nodes.label: 2grid-proj-def

nodes.name: $W^{1,\infty}$ error estimate for the Ritz projection
nodes.statement: Since $w=0$ on $\partial \Omega$ and $w$ is smooth, we have \cite[Corollary 8.1.12]{Brenner08} \begin{equation*} ||w- \hat{P}_h(w)||_{W^{1,\infty}} \leq C h^{k} ||w||_{W^{k+1,\infty}}, \ \text{for } w \in W^{k+1,\infty}(\Omega), w=0 \text{ on } \partial \Omega. \end{equation*}

nodes.name: $W^{1,\infty}$ estimate for $u-P_h u$ (defines $C_1$)
nodes.statement: ||u-P_h u||_{W^{1,\infty}} \leq C h^{k} ||u||_{W^{k+1,\infty}} \equiv C_1 h^k, \ \text{for } u \in W^{k+1,\infty}(\Omega).
nodes.label: 2grid-proj1

nodes.name: Broken $W^{2,\infty}$ estimate for $u-P_h u$
nodes.statement: ||u-P_h u||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} &\leq C h^{k-1} ||u||_{W^{k+1,\infty}} .
nodes.label: 2grid-proj2

nodes.name: Discrete Green's functions $g^z_{h,i}$ and $G^z_h$
nodes.statement: For $z\in \Omega \setminus \cup_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h}\partial K$, let $g^z_{h,i} \in V_h \cap H_0^1(\Omega)$, $i=1,2$ be defined by: \begin{equation} A'(u; g^z_{h,i},\phi)=\frac{\partial \phi}{\partial x_i}(z), \quad \forall \phi \in V_h \cap H_0^1(\Omega), \end{equation} and let $G^z_h$ be defined by \begin{equation} A'(u;G^z_h,\phi) = \phi (z), \quad \forall \phi \in V_h \cap H_0^1(\Omega). \end{equation}

nodes.name: Discrete derivative Green's function $g^z_{h,i}$
nodes.statement: A'(u; g^z_{h,i},\phi)=\frac{\partial \phi}{\partial x_i}(z), \quad \forall \phi \in V_h \cap H_0^1(\Omega),
nodes.label: 2grid-green1

nodes.name: Discrete Green's function $G^z_h$
nodes.statement: A'(u;G^z_h,\phi) = \phi (z), \quad \forall \phi \in V_h \cap H_0^1(\Omega).
nodes.label: 2grid-green2

nodes.name: $W^{1,1}$ and $L^2$ bounds on discrete Green's functions
nodes.statement: We have for $h$ sufficiently small \begin{equation} \|g^z_{h,i}\|_{W^{1,1}} \leq C |\ln h|, \end{equation} and \begin{align*} \|G^z_h\|_{L^{2}} \leq C, \end{align*} where the constant $C$ is independent of $z$.

nodes.name: Proof of the Green's function bounds (by reference)
nodes.statement: In the case $\operatorname{cof} D^2 u$ is the identity matrix, the proof is given in \cite[Lemmas 2.1 and 3.3]{ThomeeXuZhang}. The proof of the general case is similar \cite{Malitz-thesis}.
nodes.statement_short: By reference: Thomée-Xu-Zhang for the identity-coefficient case, Malitz's thesis for the general case.

nodes.name: $W^{1,1}$ bound on $G^z_h$
nodes.statement: Moreover we have \cite{Malitz-thesis}, see also \cite[Exercise 8.x.19]{Brenner08}, \begin{align} \|G^z_h\|_{W^{1,1}} \leq C|\ln h|. \end{align}

nodes.name: Proof of the $W^{1,1}$ bound on $G^z_h$
nodes.statement: It is enough to prove that $|G^z_h |_{W^{1,1}} \leq C|\ln h|$ which follows from the bound $| G^z_h |_{W^{1,2}} \leq C | \ln h|^{\frac{1}{2}} $ and H\"older's inequality. By the discrete Sobolev inequality \cite[(4.9.2)]{Brenner08} and the coercivity of the form $A'(u; .,.)$, we have for $h$ sufficiently small \begin{align*} | A'(u;G^z_h,G^z_h) | = | G^z_h (z)| \leq || G^z_h ||_{L^{\infty}} \leq C | \ln h|^{\frac{1}{2}} || G^z_h ||_{H^{1}} \leq C | \ln h|^{\frac{1}{2}} |A'(u;G^z_h,G^z_h)|^{\frac{1}{2}}. \end{align*} It follows that $$ | G^z_h |_{W^{1,2}} \leq C |A'(u;G^z_h,G^z_h)|^{\frac{1}{2}} \leq C | \ln h|^{\frac{1}{2}}, $$ giving the claimed bound.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to an $H^1$ seminorm bound via Hölder; obtain it from the discrete Sobolev inequality and coercivity of $A'(u;\cdot,\cdot)$.

nodes.name: Reduce the $W^{1,1}$ bound to an $H^1$ seminorm bound of ord
nodes.statement: It is enough to prove that $|G^z_h |_{W^{1,1}} \leq C|\ln h|$ which follows from the bound $| G^z_h |_{W^{1,2}} \leq C | \ln h|^{\frac{1}{2}} $ and H\"older's inequality.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce the $W^{1,1}$ bound to an $H^1$ seminorm bound of order $|\ln h|^{1/2}$ via Hölder

nodes.name: Bound $A'(u
nodes.statement: By the discrete Sobolev inequality \cite[(4.9.2)]{Brenner08} and the coercivity of the form $A'(u; .,.)$, we have for $h$ sufficiently small \begin{align*} | A'(u;G^z_h,G^z_h) | = | G^z_h (z)| \leq || G^z_h ||_{L^{\infty}} \leq C | \ln h|^{\frac{1}{2}} || G^z_h ||_{H^{1}} \leq C | \ln h|^{\frac{1}{2}} |A'(u;G^z_h,G^z_h)|^{\frac{1}{2}}. \end{align*}

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.1
nodes.statement: For $w,v \in H^2(K)$ for all $K \in \mathcal{T}_h$ we have \begin{multline*} A(w+v,\phi)-A(w,\phi)= -\sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h} \int_{K} \big(\det D^2(w+v)-\det D^2w\big)\phi\,d x \\+ \sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}_h^i } \int_e \[\{\!\{\operatorname{cof} D^2 (w+v) \}\!\} D (w+v) \] \phi \,d s - \sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}_h^i } \int_e \[\{\!\{\operatorname{cof} D^2 w \}\!\} D w \] \phi \,d s, \end{multline*} for all $\phi \in H^1_0(\Omega)$. Since $D^2 w$ is a $2 \times 2$ matrix, $\det D^2(w+v)= \det D^2 w + \det D^2 v +\operatorname{cof} D^2 w : D^2 v$. Thus \begin{multline*} A(w+v,\phi)-A(w,\phi)= -\sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h} \int_{K} (\det D^2v)\phi\,d x -\sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h} \int_{K} (\operatorname{cof} D^2 w: D^2v)\phi\,d x \\+ \sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}_h^i } \int_e \[\{\!\{\operatorname{cof} D^2 w \}\!\} D v \] \phi\,d s + \sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}_h^i } \int_e \[\{\!\{\operatorname{cof} D^2 v \}\!\} D w \] \phi\,d s. + \sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}_h^i } \int_e \[\{\!\{\operatorname{cof} D^2 v \}\!\} D v \] \phi\,d s. \end{multline*} By \eqref{det2} $\operatorname{cof} D^2 w: D^2 v = \operatorname{div}\big((\operatorname{cof} D^2 w) D v )$. This implies that \begin{align*} A'(w;v,\phi) & = -\sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h} \int_{K} \operatorname{div} \big((\operatorname{cof} D^2 w) D v\big) \phi \,d x + \sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}_h^i } \int_e \[\{\!\{\operatorname{cof} D^2 w \}\!\} D v \] \phi \,d s \\ & \qquad \qquad \quad + \sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}_h^i } \int_e \[\{\!\{\operatorname{cof} D^2 v \}\!\} D w \] \phi \,d s, \end{align*} and $R(w;v,\phi)$ is given by \eqref{rdef1}. By integration by parts and using the fact $\phi=0$ on $\partial \Omega$, \begin{align*} A'(w;v,\phi) & = \sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h} \int_{K} \big((\operatorname{cof} D^2 w) D v \big) \cdot D \phi \,d x - \sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}_h^i } \int_e \[(\operatorname{cof} D^2 w) D v \] \phi \,d x \\ & \qquad \qquad \quad + \sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}_h^i } \int_e \[\{\!\{\operatorname{cof} D^2 w \}\!\} D v \] \phi \,d s + \sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}_h^i } \int_e \[\{\!\{\operatorname{cof} D^2 v \}\!\} D w \] \phi \,d s . \end{align*} By \eqref{jumpaverage}, $ \[(\operatorname{cof} D^2 w) D v\] = \[\{\!\{\operatorname{cof} D^2 w \}\!\} D v \] + \[\operatorname{cof} D^2 w\] \{\!\{D v\}\!\}. $ It follows that \begin{align*} A'(w;v,\phi) & = \sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h} \int_{K }\big( (\operatorname{cof} D^2 w) D v \big) \cdot D \phi \,d x - \sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}_h^i } \int_e \[(\operatorname{cof} D^2 w)\] \{\!\{D v\}\!\} \phi \,d s \\\notag & \qquad \qquad \quad + \sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}_h^i } \int_e \[\{\!\{\operatorname{cof} D^2 v \}\!\} D w \] \phi \,d s . \end{align*} Finally, since by assumption $u \in C^3(\Omega)$, $\[(\operatorname{cof} D^2 u)\]=0$. In addition, by definition $\{\!\{\operatorname{cof} D^2 v \}\!\}$ is continuous and $Du$ is continuous by the assumption on $u$. Thus $\[\{\!\{\operatorname{cof} D^2 v \}\!\} D u \]=0$ on each interior edge. The statement about $A'(u;v,\phi)$ easily follows.

nodes.statement: For $v_h \in B_h$, we have using \eqref{Phi-def} and \eqref{2grid-proj-def} \begin{align*} \begin{split} A'(u;\Phi( v_h)- P_h u,\phi) &= A'(u;\Phi( v_h)- v_h,\phi)+A'(u; v_h- P_h u,\phi) \\ &= -A_{}( v_h,\phi) + A'(u; v_h- u,\phi) + A'(u; u - P_h u,\phi) \\ &= -A_{}( v_h,\phi) + A'(u; v_h- u,\phi) - A'(u;I_h G - G, \phi). \end{split} \end{align*} By definition of the residual \eqref{rdef0}, and since $A(u,\phi)=0$, we have $$ -A_{}( v_h,\phi) + A'(u; v_h- u,\phi) = A(u,\phi) -A_{}( v_h,\phi) + A'(u; v_h- u,\phi) = -R(u;v_h-u,\phi). $$ We conclude that \begin{align} A'(u;\Phi( v_h)- P_h u,\phi) = -R(u;v_h-u,\phi) - A'(u;I_h G - G, \phi). \end{align} Therefore, using \eqref{R1-simple}, \eqref{w11-phi} and \eqref{Frechet-at-u}, we have \begin{multline*} | A'(u;\Phi( v_h)- P_h u,\phi) | \leq C || v_h-u ||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} || v_h-u ||_{W^{1,\infty}} || \phi ||_{W^{1,1}} \\ +C || v_h-u ||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} || v_h-u ||_{W^{1,\infty}} \sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}_h^i } || \phi ||_{L^1(e)} + |A'(u;I_h G - G, \phi) | \\ \leq C h^{-1} || v_h-u ||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} || v_h-u ||_{W^{1,\infty}} || \phi ||_{W^{1,1}} + |A'(u;I_h G - G, \phi)|. \end{multline*} By definition of $B_h$, $||v_h-u||_{W^{1,\infty}} \leq C h^{k} |\ln h |$. Moreover, by triangle inequality, \eqref{2grid-proj2} and an inverse estimate $||v_h-u||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} \leq ||v_h-P_h u||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} + ||P_h u-u||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} \leq C h^{k-1} |\ln h | + C h^{k-1} \leq C h^{k-1} |\ln h | $. Thus \begin{multline*} | A'(u;\Phi( v_h)- P_h u,\phi) | \leq C h^{k-2} |\ln h | \, || \phi ||_{W^{1,1}} h^{k} |\ln h | + |A'(u;I_h G - G, \phi)| \\ \leq (C h^{k-2} |\ln h |^2 ) h^{k} || \phi ||_{W^{1,1}} + | A'(u;I_h G - G, \phi)| . \end{multline*} Taking $\phi=g^z_{h,i}$ with the estimate \eqref{2grid-W11greenbound}, and taking $\phi=G^z_h$ with the estimate \eqref{green-0}, we obtain using the definition of $C_4$ $$ \|\Phi( v_h)- P_h u\|_{W^{1,\infty}} \leq (C h^{k-2} |\ln h |^2 + C_4 ) h^{k } |\ln h|. $$ Since $C h^{k-2} |\ln h |^2 \leq C_4$ for $h$ sufficiently small and $k \geq 3$, we get $\|\Phi( v_h)- P_h u\|_{W^{1,\infty}} \leq 2 C_4 h^{k } |\ln h|$. By triangular inequality and \eqref{2grid-proj1}, the result follows.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.5
nodes.statement: For $v_h$ and $w_h$ in $B_h$, we have \begin{align*} \begin{split} A'(u;\Phi( v_h)- \Phi( w_h),\phi) &= A'(u;\Phi( v_h)- v_h,\phi)+A'(u; v_h- w_h,\phi) \\ & \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad + A'(u;w_h - \Phi( w_h),\phi)\\ &= A_{}( w_h,\phi) -A_{}( v_h,\phi) + A'(u; v_h- w_h,\phi) \\ &= A_{}( w_h,\phi) -A_{}( v_h,\phi) + A'(u; v_h -u,\phi) + A'(u; u - w_h,\phi). \end{split} \end{align*} Since $A(u,\phi)=0$, by definition of the residual \eqref{rdef0}, we have $$ A'(u;\Phi( v_h)- \Phi( w_h),\phi) = R(u;w_h-u,\phi) - R(u;v_h-u,\phi). $$ Using algebraic manipulations of the type identified in Lemma \ref{algebraic} and \eqref{R1-simple}, we obtain \begin{multline} A'(u;\Phi( v_h)- \Phi( w_h),\phi) = \frac{1}{2} \sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h} \int_K [(\operatorname{cof} D^2 (w_h - v_h) ) D (w_h - u) ] \cdot D \phi \,d x \\ + \frac{1}{2} \sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h} \int_K [(\operatorname{cof} D^2 (v_h - u) ) D (w_h - v_h) ] \cdot D \phi \,d x \\ -\frac{1}{2} \sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}_h^i } \int_e \bigg( \[(\operatorname{cof} D^2 (w_h-v_h)) \] \{\!\{ D (w_h-u) \}\!\} + \[(\operatorname{cof} D^2 (v_h-u)) \] \{\!\{ D (w_h-v_h) \}\!\} \bigg) \phi \,d s \\ + \frac{1}{2} \sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}_h^i } \int_e \bigg( \[ \{\!\{\operatorname{cof} D^2 (w_h-v_h) \}\!\} D (w_h-u) \] + \[ \{\!\{\operatorname{cof} D^2 (v_h-u) \}\!\} D (w_h-v_h) \] \bigg) \phi\,d s. \end{multline} Arguing as in the proof of Lemma \ref{invariant} and using \eqref{w11-phi}, we obtain \begin{multline*} |A'(u;\Phi( v_h)- \Phi( w_h),\phi) | \leq C \Big( || w_h- v_h||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h) } ||w_h-u||_{W^{1,\infty}} \\ + ||v_h-u||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} ||v_h-w_h ||_{W^{1,\infty}} \Big) ||\phi ||_{W^{1,1}}. \end{multline*} As in the proof of Lemma \ref{invariant}, we have $||v_h-u||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} \leq C h^{k-1} |\ln h|$ and recall that $||w_h-u||_{W^{1,\infty}} \leq C h^{k} |\ln h|$ by definition of $B_h$. Moreover, by an inverse estimate $|| w_h- v_h||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h) } \leq C h^{-1} || w_h- v_h||_{W^{1,\infty} }$. We conclude that $$ |A'(u;\Phi( v_h)- \Phi( w_h),\phi) | \leq C\big( h^{k-1} |\ln h|+h^{k-1} |\ln h| \big)||v_h-w_h ||_{W^{1,\infty}}||\phi ||_{W^{1,1}}. $$ Taking $\phi=g^z_{h,i}$ with the estimate \eqref{2grid-W11greenbound}, and taking $\phi=G^z_h$ with the estimate \eqref{green-0}, we obtain $$ \|\Phi( v_h)- \Phi( w_h) \|_{W^{1,\infty}} \leq C ( h^{k-1}+h^{k-1} )|\ln h|^2 ||v_h-w_h ||_{W^{1,\infty}}, $$ that is, for $k \geq 2$ and $h$ sufficiently small, we have $ \|\Phi( v_h)- \Phi( w_h) \|_{W^{1,\infty}} \leq 1/2 ||v_h-w_h ||_{W^{1,\infty}}$.

Since $\Phi(u_h) = u_h$, we have \begin{align} \begin{split} A'(u; u_h - P_h u,\phi) & = A'(u; \Phi(u_h) - P_h u,\phi) \\ & = A'(u; \Phi(u_h) - \Phi(P_h u),\phi) + A'(u; \Phi(P_h u) - P_h u,\phi). \end{split} \end{align} In view of \eqref{expr-con}, we obtain \begin{multline} | A'(u; \Phi(u_h) - \Phi(P_h u),\phi)| \leq C ||u_h-P_h u ||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} ||P_h u-u ||_{H^{1}} ||\phi||_{H^1} + \\ C ||u_h- u ||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} || u_h- P_h u ||_{H^{1}} ||\phi||_{H^1} + C ||u_h-P_h u ||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} \sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h } | P_h u - u |_{H^{1}(\partial K)} ||\phi||_{L^2(\partial K)} \\ + C ||u_h- u ||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} \sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h } || P_h u - u_h ||_{H^{1}(\partial K)} ||\phi||_{L^2(\partial K)}. \end{multline} By an inverse estimate, Theorem \ref{2grid-imp-thm}, triangle inequality and \eqref{2grid-proj1}, we have $||u_h-P_h u ||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} \leq C h^{k-1} | \ln h| $. Similarly, using \eqref{2grid-proj2}, we have $||u_h- u ||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} \leq C h^{k-1} | \ln h|$. Next, by the scaled trace inverse inequality \eqref{trace-inverse} and Cauchy-Schwarz inequality \begin{multline} \sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h } || P_h u - u_h ||_{H^{1}(\partial K)} ||\phi||_{L^2(\partial K)} \leq C h^{-1} \sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h } || P_h u - u_h ||_{H^{1}( K)} ||\phi||_{H^1( K)} \\ \leq C h^{-1} || P_h u - u_h ||_{H^{1}} ||\phi||_{H^1}. \end{multline} By \eqref{bramble}, an inverse estimate and \eqref{local-nodal-interpolant} \begin{align*} | P_h u - u |_{H^{1}(\partial K)} & \leq | P_h u - I_h u |_{H^{1}(\partial K)} + | I_h u - u |_{H^{1}(\partial K)} \\ & \leq C h^{-\frac{1}{2}} | P_h u - I_h u |_{H^{1}(K)} + C h^{k-\frac{1}{2}} ||u||_{H^{k+1}(K)} \\ & \leq C h^{-\frac{1}{2}} | P_h u - u |_{H^{1}(K)} + C h^{-\frac{1}{2}} | u - I_h u |_{H^{1}(K)} + C h^{k-\frac{1}{2}} ||u||_{H^{k+1}(K)}\\ & \leq C h^{-\frac{1}{2}} | P_h u - u |_{H^{1}(K)} + C h^{k-\frac{1}{2}} ||u||_{H^{k+1}(K)}. \end{align*} We have $|| P_h u - u ||_{H^{1}} \leq C h^k ||u||_{H^{k+1}}$. This follows from \cite[Theorem 5.4.4]{Brenner08} in the case of homogeneous boundary conditions. The proof of the general case is similar to \eqref{2grid-proj1}. Thus $$ \bigg( \sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h} | P_h u - u |_{H^{1}(\partial K)} ^2 \bigg)^{\frac{1}{2}} \leq C h^{-\frac{1}{2}} | P_h u - u |_{H^{1}} + C h^{k-\frac{1}{2}} ||u||_{H^{k+1}} \leq C h^{k-\frac{1}{2}} ||u||_{H^{k+1}}. $$ As with \eqref{u-p-03}, by \eqref{trace-inverse} and Cauchy-Schwarz inequality, it follows that \begin{multline} \sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h } | P_h u - u |_{H^{1}(\partial K)} ||\phi||_{L^2(\partial K)} \leq C h^{-\frac{1}{2} } \sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h } | P_h u - u |_{H^{1}(\partial K)} ||\phi||_{H^1( K)} \\ \leq C h^{k-1} ||u||_{H^{k+1} } ||\phi||_{H^1}. \end{multline} We conclude from \eqref{u-p-02}--\eqref{u-p-04} that \begin{multline*} | A'(u; \Phi(u_h) - \Phi(P_h u),\phi)| \leq C h^{k-1} | \ln h| \, || P_h u - u ||_{H^{1}} ||\phi||_{H^1} \\ + C h^{k-1} | \ln h| \, || u_h - P_h u ||_{H^{1}} ||\phi||_{H^1} + C h^{k-1} ||u_h - P_h u ||_{W^{2,\infty}} ||\phi||_{H^1} \\ + C h^{k-2} | \ln h| \, || u_h - P_h u ||_{H^{1}} ||\phi||_{H^1}. \end{multline*} Therefore since by Theorem \ref{2grid-imp-thm} we have the suboptimal estimate $ || u_h - P_h u ||_{H^{1}} \leq C ||u_h - P_h u ||_{W^{1,\infty}} \leq C h^k | \ln h| $ \begin{multline} | A'(u; \Phi(u_h) - \Phi(P_h u),\phi)| \leq C h^{k-1} | \ln h| h^k ||\phi||_{H^1} + C h^{k-1} | \ln h|^2 h^k ||\phi||_{H^1} \\ + C h^{k-2} | \ln h| h^k ||\phi||_{H^1} + C h^{k-2} | \ln h|^2 h^k ||\phi||_{H^1}\\ \leq C h^{k-2} | \ln h|^2 h^k ||\phi||_{H^1} \leq C h^k ||\phi||_{H^1}, \end{multline} for $k \geq 3$. By \eqref{expr-inv}, we have $$ A'(u; \Phi(P_h u) - P_h u,\phi) = -R(u;P_h u-u,\phi) + A'(u;I_h G - G, \phi). $$ Using \eqref{R1-simple} and inverse estimates as for \eqref{u-p-04}, we obtain \begin{multline*} | A'(u; \Phi(P_h u) - P_h u,\phi) | \leq C ||P_h u - u ||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} ||P_h u - u ||_{H^{1}} ||\phi||_{H^1} \\ + C h^{-1} ||P_h u - u ||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} || P_h u - u ||_{H^{1}} ||\phi||_{H^1} +C\|I_hG-G\|_{H^1}\|\phi\|_{H^1}, \end{multline*} i.e. \begin{multline} | A'(u; \Phi(P_h u) - P_h u,\phi) | \leq C ( h^{k-1} |\ln h| h^k + h^{k-2} |\ln h| h^k + h^k ) ||\phi||_{H^1} \\ \leq C h^k ||\phi||_{H^1}, \end{multline} for $k \geq 3$. Taking $\phi = u_h - P_h u $ in \eqref{u-p-01} and using \eqref{u-p-05} and \eqref{u-p-06}, we get from Poincar\'e's inequality and $k \geq 3$, for $h$ sufficiently small $$ || u_h - P_h u ||_{H^{1}} \leq Ch^k. $$ This completes the proof by a triangle inequality.

u_h-u^h, \phi)&= A'(u_H; u_h-u_H, \phi) + A'(u_H; u_H-u^h, \phi) \\ & = A'(u_H; u_h-u_H, \phi) + A(u_H,\phi) \\ & = A(u_h,\phi) - R(u_H;u_h-u_H,\phi) = - R(u_H;u_h-u_H,\phi). \end{align*} It follows that \begin{align*} A'(u; u_h-u^h, \phi)& = A'(u-u_H; u_h-u^h, \phi) + A'(u_H; u_h-u^h, \phi) \\ & = A'(u-u_H; u_h-u^h, \phi) - R(u_H;u_h-u_H,\phi). \end{align*} With arguments similar to the ones used in the proof of Theorem \ref{2grid-imp2-thm}, we have \begin{multline} | A'(u; u_h-u^h, \phi) | \leq C || u - u_H ||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} || u_h - u^h ||_{H^{1}} ||\phi||_{H^1} \\ + C h^{-1} || u - u_H ||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} || u_h - u^h ||_{H^{1}} ||\phi||_{H^1} + C || \phi ||_{L^{\infty}} \sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h } | u - u_H |_{H^{1}(\partial K)} || u_h - u^h ||_{H^2(\partial K)}\\ + |R(u_H;u_h-u_H,\phi)|. \end{multline} But, using \eqref{bramble}, \eqref{local-nodal-interpolant} and an inverse estimate \begin{align*} | u - u_H |_{H^{1}(\partial K)} & \leq | u - I_H u |_{H^{1}(\partial K)} + | I_H u - u_H |_{H^{1}(\partial K)} \\ & \leq C H^{k-\frac{1}{2}} ||u||_{H^{k+1}(K)} + C H^{-\frac{1}{2}} | I_H u - u_H |_{H^{1}( K)} \\ & \leq C H^{k-\frac{1}{2}} ||u||_{H^{k+1}(K)} + C H^{-\frac{1}{2}} | I_H u - u |_{H^{1}( K)} + C H^{-\frac{1}{2}} | u - u_H |_{H^{1} ( K)}. \end{align*} It follows that $$ \bigg( \sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h } | u - u_H |^2_{H^{1}(\partial K)} \bigg)^{\frac{1}{2}} \leq C H^{k-\frac{1}{2}} ||u||_{H^{k+1}} + C H^{-\frac{1}{2}} | I_H u - u |_{H^{1}} + C H^{-\frac{1}{2}} | u - u_H |_{H^{1} }. $$ We therefore obtain from \eqref{nodal-interpolant} and Theorem \ref{2grid-imp2-thm} $$ \bigg( \sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h } | u - u_H |^2_{H^{1}(\partial K)} \bigg)^{\frac{1}{2}} \leq C H^{k-\frac{1}{2}} ||u||_{H^{k+1}}. $$ By Cauchy-Schwarz's inequality, \eqref{trace-inverse} and an inverse estimate, it follows that $$ \sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h } | u - u_H |_{H^{1}(\partial K)} || u_h - u^h ||_{H^2(\partial K)} \leq C h^{- \frac{3}{2}} H^{k-\frac{1}{2}} ||u||_{H^{k+1}} || u_h - u^h ||_{H^{1}}. $$ Therefore, since $|| u - u_H ||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} \leq C H^{k-1} |\ln H|$ and by the discrete Sobolev inequality, c.f. \cite{Bramble86}, $|| \phi ||_{L^{\infty}} \leq C (1+ | \ln h|^{ 1/2 }) ||\phi||_{H^1}$, we obtain from \eqref{u-p-066} \begin{multline} | A'(u; u_h-u^h, \phi) | \leq C h^{-1} || u - u_H ||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} || u_h - u^h ||_{H^{1}} ||\phi||_{H^1} \\ + C H^{k-\frac{1}{2}} h^{- \frac{3}{2}} | \ln h| \, || u_h - u^h ||_{H^{1}} ||u||_{H^{k+1} } ||\phi||_{H^1} + |R(u_H;u_h-u_H,\phi)| \\ \leq C h^{-1} H^{k-1} |\ln H| \, || u_h - u^h ||_{H^{1}} ||\phi||_{H^1} + C H^{k-\frac{1}{2}} h^{- \frac{3}{2}} |\ln h| \, || u_h - u^h ||_{H^{1}} ||\phi||_{H^1} \\ + |R(u_H;u_h-u_H,\phi)|. \end{multline} Using \eqref{R1-simple} and the trace estimates \eqref{trace-inverse} and \eqref{trace-estimate}, we have \begin{multline} |R(u_H;u_h-u_H,\phi)| \leq C || u_h - u_H ||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} || u_h - u_H ||_{H^{1}} ||\phi||_{H^1} \\ + C h^{-1} || u_h - u_H ||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} || u_h - u_H ||_{H^{1}} ||\phi||_{H^1} \\ \leq C h^{-2} || u_h - u_H ||_{W^{1,\infty}} || u_h - u_H ||_{H^{1}} ||\phi||_{H^1}. \end{multline} Taking $\phi = u_h - u^h $ in \eqref{u-p-07} and using \eqref{u-p-08}, we get from Poincar\'e's inequality, Theorems \ref{2grid-imp-thm} and \ref{2grid-imp2-thm} for $k \geq 3$ and $h$ sufficiently small \begin{multline*} || u_h - u^h ||_{H^{1}} \leq C (h^{-1} H^{k-1} |\ln H| + H^{k-\frac{1}{2}} h^{- \frac{3}{2}} |\ln h| ) || u_h - u^h ||_{H^{1}} \\ +C h^{-2} (h^{k} |\ln h | + H^{k} |\ln H |) (h^k+H^k). \end{multline*} We conclude that for $H=h^{\lambda}$, $\lambda > \max \{1/(k-1), 3/(2k-1) \} = 3/(2k-1)$ and $k \geq 3$, $$ || u_h - u^h ||_{H^{1}} \leq C h^{-2} |\ln H \, | H^{2k}. $$ We therefore get $||u^h-u_h||_{H^{1}} \leq C h^k$ provided $\lambda > 3/(2k-1)$ and $2 \lambda k -2- \epsilon > k$ for some $\epsilon \in (0,1) $, that is $\lambda > \max \{ (k+2+ \epsilon)/(2k), 3/(2k-1) \} = 1/2 + (2+\epsilon)/(2k)$ for $k \geq 3$.
nodes.statement_short: Derive an error equation for $u_h-u^h$ from the Newton step and the Taylor remainder, then bound coefficient perturbation and remainder terms. Testing with $u_h-u^h$ and choosing $H=h^\lambda$ absorbs the error.

nodes.name: Error equation for $u_h-u^h$ with the coarse linearization
nodes.statement: By definition of the two-grid algorithm, the definition of the residual \eqref{rdef0}, and $A(u_h,\phi)=0$ for $\phi \in V_h\cap W^{1,\infty}_0(\Omega)$, we have \begin{align*} A'(u_H; u_h-u^h, \phi)&= A'(u_H; u_h-u_H, \phi) + A'(u_H; u_H-u^h, \phi) \\ & = A'(u_H; u_h-u_H, \phi) + A(u_H,\phi) \\ & = A(u_h,\phi) - R(u_H;u_h-u_H,\phi) = - R(u_H;u_h-u_H,\phi). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Error equation for $u_h-u^h$ with the coarse linearization

nodes.name: Switch to the exact-solution linearization plus a perturbati
nodes.statement: It follows that \begin{align*} A'(u; u_h-u^h, \phi)& = A'(u-u_H; u_h-u^h, \phi) + A'(u_H; u_h-u^h, \phi) \\ & = A'(u-u_H; u_h-u^h, \phi) - R(u_H;u_h-u_H,\phi). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Switch to the exact-solution linearization plus a perturbation term

nodes.name: Bound the error equation (4.2)
nodes.statement: With arguments similar to the ones used in the proof of Theorem \ref{2grid-imp2-thm}, we have \begin{multline} | A'(u; u_h-u^h, \phi) | \leq C || u - u_H ||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} || u_h - u^h ||_{H^{1}} ||\phi||_{H^1} \\ + C h^{-1} || u - u_H ||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} || u_h - u^h ||_{H^{1}} ||\phi||_{H^1} + C || \phi ||_{L^{\infty}} \sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h } | u - u_H |_{H^{1}(\partial K)} || u_h - u^h ||_{H^2(\partial K)}\\ + |R(u_H;u_h-u_H,\phi)|. \end{multline}
nodes.statement_short: Bound the error equation (4.2)

nodes.name: Elementwise bound on $|u-u_H|_{H^1(\partial K)}$
nodes.statement: But, using \eqref{bramble}, \eqref{local-nodal-interpolant} and an inverse estimate \begin{align*} | u - u_H |_{H^{1}(\partial K)} & \leq | u - I_H u |_{H^{1}(\partial K)} + | I_H u - u_H |_{H^{1}(\partial K)} \\ & \leq C H^{k-\frac{1}{2}} ||u||_{H^{k+1}(K)} + C H^{-\frac{1}{2}} | I_H u - u_H |_{H^{1}( K)} \\ & \leq C H^{k-\frac{1}{2}} ||u||_{H^{k+1}(K)} + C H^{-\frac{1}{2}} | I_H u - u |_{H^{1}( K)} + C H^{-\frac{1}{2}} | u - u_H |_{H^{1} ( K)}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Elementwise bound on $|u-u_H|_{H^1(\partial K)}$

nodes.name: Sum and use interpolation and Theorem 3.7
nodes.statement: It follows that $$ \bigg( \sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h } | u - u_H |^2_{H^{1}(\partial K)} \bigg)^{\frac{1}{2}} \leq C H^{k-\frac{1}{2}} ||u||_{H^{k+1}} + C H^{-\frac{1}{2}} | I_H u - u |_{H^{1}} + C H^{-\frac{1}{2}} | u - u_H |_{H^{1} }. $$ We therefore obtain from \eqref{nodal-interpolant} and Theorem \ref{2grid-imp2-thm} $$ \bigg( \sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h } | u - u_H |^2_{H^{1}(\partial K)} \bigg)^{\frac{1}{2}} \leq C H^{k-\frac{1}{2}} ||u||_{H^{k+1}}. $$
nodes.statement_short: Sum and use interpolation and Theorem 3.7

nodes.name: Bound the boundary product term
nodes.statement: By Cauchy-Schwarz's inequality, \eqref{trace-inverse} and an inverse estimate, it follows that $$ \sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h } | u - u_H |_{H^{1}(\partial K)} || u_h - u^h ||_{H^2(\partial K)} \leq C h^{- \frac{3}{2}} H^{k-\frac{1}{2}} ||u||_{H^{k+1}} || u_h - u^h ||_{H^{1}}. $$
nodes.statement_short: Bound the boundary product term

nodes.name: Discrete Sobolev inequality gives (4.3)
nodes.statement: Therefore, since $|| u - u_H ||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} \leq C H^{k-1} |\ln H|$ and by the discrete Sobolev inequality, c.f. \cite{Bramble86}, $|| \phi ||_{L^{\infty}} \leq C (1+ | \ln h|^{ 1/2 }) ||\phi||_{H^1}$, we obtain from \eqref{u-p-066} \begin{multline} | A'(u; u_h-u^h, \phi) | \leq C h^{-1} || u - u_H ||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} || u_h - u^h ||_{H^{1}} ||\phi||_{H^1} \\ + C H^{k-\frac{1}{2}} h^{- \frac{3}{2}} | \ln h| \, || u_h - u^h ||_{H^{1}} ||u||_{H^{k+1} } ||\phi||_{H^1} + |R(u_H;u_h-u_H,\phi)| \\ \leq C h^{-1} H^{k-1} |\ln H| \, || u_h - u^h ||_{H^{1}} ||\phi||_{H^1} + C H^{k-\frac{1}{2}} h^{- \frac{3}{2}} |\ln h| \, || u_h - u^h ||_{H^{1}} ||\phi||_{H^1} \\ + |R(u_H;u_h-u_H,\phi)|. \end{multline}
nodes.statement_short: Discrete Sobolev inequality gives (4.3)

nodes.name: Bound the coarse remainder (4.4)
nodes.statement: Using \eqref{R1-simple} and the trace estimates \eqref{trace-inverse} and \eqref{trace-estimate}, we have \begin{multline} |R(u_H;u_h-u_H,\phi)| \leq C || u_h - u_H ||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} || u_h - u_H ||_{H^{1}} ||\phi||_{H^1} \\ + C h^{-1} || u_h - u_H ||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} || u_h - u_H ||_{H^{1}} ||\phi||_{H^1} \\ \leq C h^{-2} || u_h - u_H ||_{W^{1,\infty}} || u_h - u_H ||_{H^{1}} ||\phi||_{H^1}. \end{multline}
nodes.statement_short: Bound the coarse remainder (4.4)

nodes.name: Test with $u_h-u^h$ and apply Poincaré with Theorems 3.6, 3.
nodes.statement: Taking $\phi = u_h - u^h $ in \eqref{u-p-07} and using \eqref{u-p-08}, we get from Poincar\'e's inequality, Theorems \ref{2grid-imp-thm} and \ref{2grid-imp2-thm} for $k \geq 3$ and $h$ sufficiently small \begin{multline*} || u_h - u^h ||_{H^{1}} \leq C (h^{-1} H^{k-1} |\ln H| + H^{k-\frac{1}{2}} h^{- \frac{3}{2}} |\ln h| ) || u_h - u^h ||_{H^{1}} \\ +C h^{-2} (h^{k} |\ln h | + H^{k} |\ln H |) (h^k+H^k). \end{multline*}
nodes.statement_short: Test with $u_h-u^h$ and apply Poincaré with Theorems 3.6, 3.7

nodes.name: Choose $\lambda$ to absorb and obtain the $O(h^k)$ bound
nodes.statement: We conclude that for $H=h^{\lambda}$, $\lambda > \max \{1/(k-1), 3/(2k-1) \} = 3/(2k-1)$ and $k \geq 3$, $$ || u_h - u^h ||_{H^{1}} \leq C h^{-2} |\ln H \, | H^{2k}. $$ We therefore get $||u^h-u_h||_{H^{1}} \leq C h^k$ provided $\lambda > 3/(2k-1)$ and $2 \lambda k -2- \epsilon > k$ for some $\epsilon \in (0,1) $, that is $\lambda > \max \{ (k+2+ \epsilon)/(2k), 3/(2k-1) \} = 1/2 + (2+\epsilon)/(2k)$ for $k \geq 3$.
nodes.statement_short: Choose $\lambda$ to absorb and obtain the $O(h^k)$ bound

nodes.name: Bound on $A'(u;u_h-u^h,\phi)$
nodes.statement: | A'(u; u_h-u^h, \phi) | \leq C || u - u_H ||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} || u_h - u^h ||_{H^{1}} ||\phi||_{H^1} \\ + C h^{-1} || u - u_H ||_{W^{2,\infty}(\mathcal{T}_h)} || u_h - u^h ||_{H^{1}} ||\phi||_{H^1} + C || \phi ||_{L^{\infty}} \sum_{K \in \mathcal{T}_h } | u - u_H |_{H^{1}(\partial K)} || u_h - u^h ||_{H^2(\partial K)}\\ + |R(u_H;u_h-u_H,\phi)|.
nodes.label: u-p-066

nodes.name: Smooth convex test function
nodes.statement: We consider a smooth convex test function $u(x,y)=e^{(x^2+y^2)/2}$ so that $f(x,y)=(1+x^2+y^2)e^{(x^2+y^2)}$ and $g(x,y)=e^{(x^2+y^2)/2}$ on $\partial \Omega$.

nodes.name: Convergence for quadratic elements
nodes.statement: While our convergence analysis is only for cubic and higher order elements, we believe the results should be true for quadratic elements.
conclusions: the results should be true for quadratic elements

nodes.name: Coarse-grid Newton solver with Poisson initial guess
nodes.statement: On the coarse grid of size $H$, we first seek an initial guess $u_H^0$ of $u_H$ as the standard finite element approximation of the solution $u_0$ of \begin{equation*} \Delta u_0=2\sqrt{f}, \quad u_0=g \text{ on } \partial \Omega. \end{equation*} For solving the coarse grid problem, we perform Newton's method on the coarse grid, setting the maximum iterations to 10 and we impose that the algorithm terminates when $\|u_H\|_{L^{\infty}}/ \|u^0_H\|_{L^{\infty}} \leq 10^{-6}.$
nodes.statement_short: Initialize with the finite element solution of $\Delta u_0=2\sqrt f$, then run at most 10 Newton iterations on the coarse grid with a relative stopping test.

nodes.name: Poisson initial guess
nodes.statement: On the coarse grid of size $H$, we first seek an initial guess $u_H^0$ of $u_H$ as the standard finite element approximation of the solution $u_0$ of \begin{equation*} \Delta u_0=2\sqrt{f}, \quad u_0=g \text{ on } \partial \Omega. \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Initial guess from the Poisson problem $\Delta u_0=2\sqrt f$

nodes.name: Coarse Newton iterations with stopping test
nodes.statement: For solving the coarse grid problem, we perform Newton's method on the coarse grid, setting the maximum iterations to 10 and we impose that the algorithm terminates when $\|u_H\|_{L^{\infty}}/ \|u^0_H\|_{L^{\infty}} \leq 10^{-6}.$
nodes.statement_short: Newton's method, at most 10 iterations, stop on relative $L^\infty$ criterion

nodes.name: Further experiments: $P_3$, multigrid, second fine-grid iteration
nodes.statement: Experiments with $P_3$ elements gave the expected results, and so we do not report those here. We also attempted several multigrid experiments, where we interpolate between a series of meshes before ending on the fine grid. However these gave results comparable to the two-grid algorithm. At the cost of extra computation time, there is a slight increase in accuracy if a second iteration is performed on the fine grid. We do not report these results since a second iteration on the fine grid does not affect the rate of convergence of the method.
nodes.statement_short: $P_3$ results as expected; multigrid variants comparable; a second fine Newton step improves accuracy slightly without changing the rate.

nodes.name: Two-grid computations are accurate and fast
nodes.statement: The two-grid computations are accurate and fast compared with Newton's method.
